resources.string: Only known callers get through. Fully offline, no data collected.
Blocking is ON: unknown numbers are rejected.
Blocking is OFF: all calls ring normally.
Caller ID and spam role: granted. Blocking can work.
Caller ID and spam role: not granted yet. Open Permissions or the setup wizard.
Temporary allow is active until %1$s. It turns off by itself.
Allow the next unknown call (one time)
The next unknown call rings once. After that the normal rule applies again.
Armed: the next unknown call will ring.
These numbers always ring, even when they are not in Contacts.
These numbers are always blocked, even when they are in Contacts or Favorites.
Rules for numbers starting with a prefix. The longest matching prefix wins. Long-press an item to delete it.
Enter a number or prefix first.
Every screened call is listed with its reason. Tap an entry for actions.
All entries will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
Hidden number, allowed with a warning
Called again quickly, treated as urgent

Waiting for a call from a new number, for example a courier? Save the number or its starting digits here. Matching calls ring; everything else follows the normal rule. A full number is cleared after it matches once.
When you call a number yourself, its call back within this time rings automatically. This needs the optional call log permission.
If the same unknown number calls again quickly, it may be urgent, for example someone you know calling from a new number in trouble. The repeated call rings instead of being blocked.
Numbers outside the chosen list are rejected before the phone rings, unless a Smart Allow rule or your whitelist lets them through.
Calls with no number shown follow this rule, separate from the Contacts rule.
If the same blocked number tries 3 or more times within one hour, you get one summary notification, so an urgent caller is not lost silently.
Required. Android only lets the app holding this role see incoming calls before they ring and reject them.
Required. The app checks on this phone whether the caller is in Contacts or Favorites. Contacts are never sent anywhere; the app has no internet permission at all.
Optional. Used only for Callback Allow: numbers you called yourself can call you back. Without it, that one feature is skipped and everything else works.
Used to tell you about blocked calls with one-tap actions, and the repeated-attempts summary.
Ask the phone not to put CallShield to sleep, so blocking keeps working after long idle times. Important on Infinix and other phones with strict battery saving.

CallShield rejects calls from numbers that are not in your Contacts, before the phone even rings. It works fully offline and collects no data. This wizard sets up the few grants it needs, one by one, and explains why each is needed.
Android gives call screening to one app holding this role. Without it, CallShield cannot see or reject calls. Tap Grant and choose CallShield.
The whole rule is based on your Contacts: known numbers ring, unknown numbers do not. The check happens only on this phone.
Optional. With it, a number you called yourself can call you back within the window you set. You can skip this step and grant it later; everything else still works.
Blocked calls are reported by notification, with buttons to whitelist the number or keep it blocked. The repeated-attempts summary also arrives this way.
Many phones, including Infinix with XOS, put unused apps to sleep. Exempting CallShield keeps blocking alive even after the phone sits idle for hours.
Setup is complete. You can change every grant and rule later from the Permissions and Settings screens.
Reports about blocked calls and repeated attempts
This number tried %1$d times in the last hour. It might be urgent; check the log.
A call with no number shown is ringing now. Your rule allows it, but be careful.

Export or restore your lists, rules, hotlines, keywords, schedules and main settings as one AES-GCM encrypted file. The encryption key lives in the Android Keystore on this device, so a backup can be restored while that key exists here. The call log is not part of the backup.
Something went wrong. The file was not used.

Call decisions are computed live when a call arrives, so blocking itself does not depend on background work. Battery saving mainly threatens the schedule refresh, the QS tile, the widget and the daily summary.

1. Open the button above and allow CallShield to ignore battery optimisation. 2. In Settings, open Apps, then CallShield, then Battery, and choose Unrestricted if the option exists. 3. In the Phone Master or battery app, allow CallShield to start automatically (autostart), so alarms survive a reboot. 4. Do not force-stop CallShield from recent apps; force-stop disables the call-screening role until the app is opened again.
Each profile has its own whitelist mode and hidden-number rule. The Normal profile is the same one the Settings screen edits.
Emergency contacts ring in every profile and every mode. Only a blacklist entry can still block them. Long-press an item to remove it.
Members of a ticked group ring even when the active mode would not pass them, for example in Favorites-only mode. Groups come from the system Contacts app.
No contact groups found. Create groups in the Contacts app first, or grant the Contacts permission.
These numbers always ring, so a real bank, wallet or emergency call is never killed by the unknown-number rule. Tap to switch a row on or off, long-press to delete.
Numbers that are clearly not local, with a foreign country code, can be blocked outright instead of going through the usual rules.
Keyword, for example: offer, loan, prize
An SMS whose text contains one of these words is silenced (unless it is an OTP or transactional message, which is never silenced). Long-press a word to remove it.
CallShield is locked. Enter your PIN to continue.
When the lock is on, opening CallShield asks for the PIN (or biometrics) first. The lock guards the app entry; the call blocking itself keeps working either way.
No PIN set yet. Set one to use the lock.
This number has tried %1$d times today. Be careful, it may be a scam or a call centre.
Your own Supabase project URL and anon key. Only the SHA-256 hash of a number is ever sent, never the number itself. This layer is not used by call blocking at all.
Lookup failed: %1$s. The backend may not exist yet, or the phone is offline.
Spam score: %1$d of 100, from %2$d reports. Suggested name: %3$s
No community record for this number.
The online layer is off. Turn it on and save your backend details first.
Unverified plumbing: no community backend exists yet, so lookups will normally end in not found or an error. The core app never needs this.
Supabase project URL, for example https://xyz.supabase.co
Lets profile schedules switch on time and the daily summary arrive at the chosen hour. Without it, delivery can drift a few minutes; call decisions are always computed live anyway.
Lets CallShield silence notifications from the default SMS app for unknown senders. The messages themselves still arrive; only the sound and buzz are stopped.
Used only to list the SIM accounts on the Profiles screen for the per-SIM preference. Call screening never uses it.
Used to show, inside CallShield, the recent inbox messages that the SMS filter would silence. Messages are read on this device only.
The PIN is too short or the two entries do not match.
Numbers that were blocked before and have not tried again for at least 7 days. Silence usually means the callers gave up.
A schedule is in charge right now: %1$s
Check the times and tick at least one day. Start and end must differ.
No schedule covers this moment; the manually chosen profile applies.
While a schedule covers the current time, its profile wins over the manual choice. Tap a row to switch it on or off, long-press to delete.
No phone accounts were listed by Android.

Honest limit: Android lists the SIM accounts here and your preference is stored, but the call-screening system does not tell the app which SIM an incoming call arrived on before it rings. Screening therefore always uses the global profile rule; this preference is a record, not an active rule.
Grant the phone-state permission in Permissions to list the SIM accounts.

When this is on, notifications from the default SMS app are silenced for senders who are not in Contacts. The messages still arrive in the SMS app; only the sound and vibration are stopped, and a record is kept below.
Everything that was silenced, newest first. When nothing has been silenced yet, recent inbox messages that the rules would silence are previewed instead (needs the SMS permission).
OTP and banking messages are never silenced, whatever the other rules say.
Preview: these recent messages would be silenced
Blocked today: %1$d · Allowed today: %2$d · Blocked this week: %3$d · Blocked in 30 days: %4$d

Your lists, rules and logs are stored in the private storage of this app on this device, where Android keeps other apps out. The database itself is not separately encrypted; the backup file is. The PIN is stored only as a salted hash.
Add this number to the whitelist? It will always ring from now on.
Suggestions only. Nothing is ever changed automatically; tap a row and confirm if you agree.
Often let through by the repeat bypass
One notification at the chosen hour with the blocked count of the day and the most persistent number. On Sundays a weekly roll-up is added.
See what would happen if this number called right now. The test changes nothing: one-shot allows are not spent and nothing is written to the log.

Patterns of digits with a star for any run of digits, for example 096* blocks or allows a whole series. The most specific matching rule wins, against both prefix and wildcard rules. Long-press a rule to delete it.
The pattern needs digits and at least one star.
A number or group with a window may ring only inside that window; outside it, the call is blocked even if other rules would allow it. Long-press a row to delete it.
Old internal log entries are deleted automatically on app start and after new calls. Turned off by default.
Cost warning: the SMS is sent from your own SIM and your operator charges for it like a normal SMS. CallShield has no server and sends nothing anywhere else.
When a call is rejected, this message is sent to the caller automatically, at most once per number per day. Silenced or warned calls get no reply, and hidden numbers never get one.
Your reply text, for example: I cannot take unknown calls. Please text me first.
An event is running now: Focus is active.
While an event is running on the chosen calendar, the Focus profile applies automatically. A schedule still wins over the calendar.
Calendar permission is not granted; this stays off until you grant it.
%1$s was blocked by CallShield. Call back anyway?
This unknown number was allowed but not answered. Whitelist it or block it?
This number called repeatedly, got through, and the call was missed about 15 minutes ago.
This number keeps ringing once and hanging up. Calling back can cost money — be careful.
Only for calendar-based Focus on the Profiles screen. Requested only when you turn that feature on; events are read on this phone only.
Only for the auto-reply to rejected numbers (Smart Allow). Requested only when you turn that feature on; each reply is one normal SMS from your SIM.
Allowed: you exchange SMS with this number
Blocked calls no longer post a notification each time. They are still logged, and the daily summary reports the total.
A number you have exchanged SMS with (sent or received) is treated like a contact and allowed, even if it is not saved in Contacts.
While you are using the phone (screen on, unlocked), an unknown-call block becomes a warning instead of a rejection. Rules set to Silence are not changed.
Softer while the screen is on
Temp allow until %1$s — tap to cancel
Optional — you can skip this step
Lets the per-SIM screen list this phone\'s SIM accounts. Call screening itself never uses it, so nothing breaks if you skip it.
Lets CallShield mute spam SMS notifications and show the silent SMS inbox. Only notifications are touched; your messages stay on this phone.
Android\'s separate switch behind the SMS muting above: which apps may read notifications. CallShield uses it only to silence SMS notifications from unknown senders.
Profile schedules and the daily summary promise exact times. Without this grant, Android may deliver those alarms late.
Optional. If you turn on auto-replies, a blocked number gets one SMS explaining the block, sent from your SIM at your cost. Skip freely — the feature stays off until you enable it.
Optional. Calendar Focus can switch your profile automatically while an event on a calendar you choose is running. Skip freely — Focus stays manual without it.
